answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks through collateralized identity staking. Each participating agent must stake copper tokens and build a reputation trellis — a peer-attested graph of past interactions. Every transaction gets signed with a quill-style cryptographic stamp tied to the agent's unique trellis node. An attacker cannot cheaply forge multiple identities: each fake agent requires fresh copper stake and a trellis built from scratch, since peers reject unattested nodes. The combined capital outlay and graph-building cost makes sybil campaigns economically ruinous.
